 | t_heterogeneous_scheduler | unset | pass | 2 | 2,715 | 0.4 | 0
 | t_heterogeneous_scheduler | 1 | pass | 2 | 2,715 | 0.4 | 7 (one real model state prints its report)

 | t_llama_unit | 1 | pass | 62 | 220,158 | 2.5 | 126
 | t_llama_unit | yes | pass | 62 | 220,158 | 3.1 | 98, plus 7 'ignored' warning lines

Every binary prints two 'hwloc_set_cpubind for thread failed' error lines at start. They come from the container's CPU binding, are present with and without the PR, and are unrelated to the PR.

Method details

Tools: four Workflow runs with Claude subagents. Main review: 2 mapping agents (test table, change map), 12 first-round lenses, 1 merge planner, 3 refuters per merged finding (87 first-round findings), 1 completeness critic, 7 second-round lenses, 1 merge planner, 3 refuters per finding (19 second-round findings); 344 agents in all. The final synthesis agent of that run could not emit the full report within its output limit, so the report data was assembled in code from the journal (merge plan applied, refuter corrections applied by majority) and six smaller agents wrote the triage, overview, counter audit, conditions table, proposed tests and verified-correct list; two refuters checked the two tables that make new claims. Test-data check: 4 lenses, 17 findings, 2 refuters each, 1 synthesis (39 agents). Build and test: the head was built and its four test binaries were run on claude-box by the orchestrator (details under 'Tests actually run'). Every line number was read at the head by the agent that cites it; the orchestrator did not re-verify every citation, and the 'verifier notes' fields carry the refuters' caveats.
Rules applied to the prose: the plain-English rules of the reviewer's configuration (define terms at first use, one claim per sentence, units on numbers, citations after the sentence, a short version first, no idioms). A separate check pass over this page ran after generation; its corrections are already applied.
